title: Identifying sensitive information and using admin controls

opening.headline: Whether it is okay to paste an Excel file containing a customer's name into AI can only be determined by knowing what the judgment before input and the administrator's control are responsible for.
body: I would like to summarize an excel sheet containing the names, phone numbers, and purchase amounts of 100 customers. The fastest way is to copy the entire table and paste it into the dialog. However, it contains information that can identify specific individuals. What should I judge before pasting?

In this class, you will learn the classification framework for dividing data into public, internal, and sensitive, as well as de-identification, which makes individuals unrecognizable. Next, distinguish between what the administrator control can block and what it cannot, and determine step by step how much can be entered in the customer data summary case.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain types of sensitive information and input judgment criteria
Administrator control functions can distinguish between what is blocked and what is not.

screens.title: Excel sheet with customer name, can I paste it as is?
screens.lead: Read the scene below and think about what to check before pasting.

visual.alt: A scene where an Excel table containing the customer's name, phone number, and purchase amount is about to be pasted into the AI dialog input box.

paragraphs: I'd like to summarize the purchases of 100 customers last quarter. The Excel contains the name, phone number, and purchase amount. You can get the summary the fastest by copying the entire table and pasting it into the chat window.

However, this table contains information that can identify specific individuals. If your name and phone number are included, it will be clear who made the purchase. We have not considered whether this information is absolutely necessary for the purpose of the summary.
The topic of this lesson is what to judge before pasting. No matter how well the service is set up, it is ultimately up to the person to decide what to include.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: Which columns in this table really need to be summarized? We will judge again at the end of class.

screens.outro: To establish a standard for judgment, let me start by recalling my work data.

screens.title: My work data that would be difficult to export
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You won't have to enter or submit your answer, so think about it in your head first and then press it.

items.prompt: What of my current work materials would be difficult to export?
items.answer: Customer information, employee information, financial figures, contracts, and source code are common examples. The more difficult the data feels to be exposed to the outside world, the more careful judgment is needed before putting it into AI. This intuition is the starting point for classification.

items.prompt: Conversely, what data is safe to disclose?
items.answer: This applies to press releases and website text that have already been released. Not all materials need to be treated equally. Dividing the material into parts helps you focus your attention where you need to be careful.

items.prompt: Do you remember the last time you put that data into AI?
items.answer: Experiences of inadvertent pasting are common. What matters is what standard you used to make your decision at the time. If there were no standards, the classification to be established in this class and the confirmation before input would become the standards.

screens.outro: Let’s take a closer look at the criteria for dividing data.

screens.title: Classifying Sensitive Information: What is Sensitive?
screens.lead: The table below divides the data into three classes and provides examples and input judgments for each class. Read along the lines to see how confirmation before entering changes as you move up the level.

data.caption: Three levels of sensitivity of data
rows: Press releases and website text already released externally
Since it has no impact if leaked, you can enter it relatively freely in approved tools.
Business memos and general meeting materials that do not need to be disclosed to the outside world but have limited impact from being leaked
Process it in your organization's approved accounts and tools, and check retention and learning terms of use.
Information that can identify a specific individual, financial/contract/certification information, trade secrets
In principle, it is not included, or only the parts necessary for the purpose are de-identified and processed only in an approved environment.
Data that combines otherwise ordinary items such as name, contact information, and purchase history
Even if individual items are ordinary, when combined they can identify an individual, so they are classified as sensitive based on whether they are combined.
data.notes: The actual classification criteria will depend on the organization's policies and legal requirements. This table is a starting point to help you make decisions before entering. When deciding on a grade, first think about who will be harmed when the data is released to the outside world, and remember that the same data can be lowered by entering only the necessary parts depending on the purpose.

screens.outro: Now that we have divided the levels, let's look at the verification and de-identification that goes through before entering sensitive data.

screens.title: Verification and de-identification before input: before and after
screens.lead: Select the two states alternately to compare the same customer's purchase history before and after being hidden.

visual.alt: A side-by-side illustration of customer tables before and after covering.
labels: Double-check that you can't guess who it is by combining the remaining rows.

states.label: Before covering up
states.body: The original table includes name, phone number, address, purchase amount, and number of purchases. Before entering, we check two things: First, is there information in this data that can identify individuals? Second, is the information absolutely necessary for the purpose of summary? All you need for the summary are analytical columns such as purchase amount and number of purchases, name and phone number are not needed. If you paste it in this state, unnecessary identification information will also be entered.

states.label: After covering it
states.body: Change the names to random symbols such as Customer A or Customer B, and remove phone numbers and addresses or shorten them to geographic areas. Leave the columns needed for analysis, such as purchase amount and number of purchases. After receiving the results, reverting the symbol back to the person's name is done by a human by comparing it with the original within the organization. Check once more to see if you can guess who it is by combining the remaining columns even after covering them. This is because an unusual combination of location and purchase amount can reveal an individual.

screens.outro: Now that we've established the judgment of the person typing, let's look at the role that administrator controls play.

screens.title: What Admin Control Prevents and Does Not Prevent
screens.lead: Select each tab to see what admin controls determine and what they cannot determine for you.

tabs.label: OpenAI Administrator Control
tabs.body: Administrators determine which apps and plugins can be used, what operations are allowed, and access by role. The OpenAI admin documentation distinguishes between app access, i.e. who can use the connected app, and app permissions, i.e. when ChatGPT asks before using the app, into different controls. Installation of plugins and access to apps within them are also evaluated separately.

tabs.label: Google Admin Controls
tabs.body: Google administrators can turn Gemini features on and off for individual services, such as Gmail, Drive, and Docs. However, even if Gemini is turned off in one app, there are cases where the user uses Gemini in another app and accesses the data of the turned off app. For example, you can ask Gemini for Drive files in Gmail. Gemini only writes content to which users already have access, and follows existing data protection controls even when the creation is placed in a document or email.

tabs.label: What can't be prevented
tabs.body: Administrator controls determine which tools can be accessed and which features and actions are permitted. However, it does not determine for you what the user pastes into the permitted tools. Settings may not prevent you from pasting tables with customer names into approved tools. So pre-input judgment is the strongest control that precedes any other control.

screens.outro: Now that we've distinguished between the two roles of control, let's apply them to an example.

screens.title: Commentary: Customer data summary, how much can be entered?
screens.lead: The instructor will step through the customer's purchase history summary request. Select the right arrow to proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Confirm request
steps.body: The request is to summarize customer purchases for the past quarter. The data is the Excel we saw earlier. You must first determine whether it contains your name and phone number and can be pasted as is.

steps.title: Level 1 classification
steps.body: We classify this as sensitive because it contains name and contact information. Even if individual items are ordinary, the combination of name, contact information, and purchase history can make an individual identifiable.

steps.title: Step 2 Purpose
steps.body: What you need in your summary are trends by purchase amount, item, and region. Who bought it is not necessary for the summary results. It is safest not to include sensitive information in the first place if it is not necessary for the purpose.

steps.title: 3-step de-identification
steps.body: Delete the Name and Contact columns, and replace the customer number with a random symbol. Regions are broadly reduced to city or province units. Leave analytical columns such as purchase amount and item.

steps.title: Level 4 environment
steps.body: Process only from accounts and tools approved by your organization. Check the account's retention period, learning terms and conditions, and administrator settings. The principle is not to include even de-identified data in unauthorized personal accounts.

steps.title: Step 5: Archive results
steps.body: Make sure that there are no personally identifiable expressions in the summary results before sharing them. When a specific customer reappears in the results, the same problem recurs. Checking both input and output is a complete judgment.

screens.outro: Next, we will summarize questions to ask when judgment is ambiguous.

screens.title: Commentary: Questions when judgment is ambiguous
screens.lead: As you select each question, the instructor's explanation will unfold. When you encounter material with unclear boundaries, ask these questions in order.

items.prompt: Can you achieve your goal without this material?
items.answer: If possible, omit that data and enter it. The safest input is not to input it. If you don't need names in your summary, clear the name column and start from the beginning.

items.prompt: Is it handled by accounts and settings permitted by the organization?
items.answer: Even for the same material, the conditions for preservation and learning use vary depending on which account it is stored in. Check whether the account is approved by your organization and what settings your administrator has set.

items.prompt: Will the results reveal any personal or trade secrets?
items.answer: Even if you hide the input, the results can reveal a specific individual or business partner by combining the remaining information. We check the results one more time against the same criteria before sharing them.

items.prompt: What to do if you're not sure?
items.answer: Confirm with the responsible department without entering it. Judgment before input is the strongest control before any other control, so when in doubt, it is safer to stop.

screens.outro: Now that we've organized the judgment questions, let's go over the main points of the class.

screens.title: Key takeaway: Judgment before input is the strongest control.
screens.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class. Recall the customer Excel you saw at the beginning and read it again.

paragraphs: Sensitive information is divided into public, internal, and sensitive, and we look at whether individual items are revealed as well as when combined. De-identification involves erasing or changing identifying information, leaving only the rows necessary for the purpose, and checking again to see if someone can be guessed from the remaining rows even after masking.

Administrator controls determine which tools can be accessed and what actions are allowed, but they do not determine for you what users paste. Therefore, the correct decision is to omit the name and phone number in the first customer Excel and enter only the necessary columns in an approved environment.

callout.label: standards to remember
callout.text: Judgment before input is the strongest control. If you are not sure, check without entering it.

checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded.
checks.q: If an administrator has set up all Gemini features and app access, what is the best risk that remains?
options: Settings do not determine for you what users paste into permitted tools.
Access by role determined by the administrator does not apply to the user.
Placing a creation into a document removes any existing data protection controls.
Administrator settings can only be turned on and off on an app-by-app basis, making detailed control impossible.
checks.explain: Administrator controls determine which apps and tasks can be used, but they don't determine the sensitivity of what you paste. So judgment before input is the strongest control.

wrong.1: Role-specific access is a key feature of administrator controls.
wrong.2: Gemini follows existing data protection controls even when you place your work in a document or email.
wrong.3: OpenAI handles role access, tasks, and permissions in detail by dividing them into different controls.

checks.intro: Try to put your judgment process in the right order. Results are not recorded.
checks.q: Put the decision process in the right order before summarizing customer purchase history.
items: Classify as sensitive as it has name and contact information
Determine the purpose of what information is essential for the summary
Delete name/contact columns and replace customer number with random symbol
Process only from accounts and tools approved by your organization
Make sure there are no personally identifiable expressions in the results before sharing
checks.explain: We identify risks through classification, de-identify them to ensure only what is needed for the purpose, then process them in an approved environment and verify the results.

glossary.def: It is a framework for dividing data according to the impact of leakage, such as public, internal, or sensitive.
This is a process that erases personally identifiable information such as name and contact information or changes it to random symbols.
This is a procedure to check whether identifying information is included and whether it is necessary for the purpose before pasting.
This is the extent to which the organization's administrators determine apps, features, and access permissions.

misconceptions.myth: De-identification is completed by simply deleting the name.
misconceptions.fact: If you combine the remaining columns, you may be able to guess who it is. Unusual combinations of region, purchase amount, and number of purchases may reveal an individual, so we check the remaining information even after masking.

misconceptions.myth: Since the administrator has set it up, it is safe no matter what you put in it.
misconceptions.fact: Administrator controls determine access, functions, and actions. Since we do not judge what the user pastes, it is up to the user to make decisions before entering.

misconceptions.myth: If you turn off a feature in one app, all data access for that app is blocked.
misconceptions.fact: According to Google documentation, even if you turn off Gemini in one app, other apps will still be able to access that app's data when you use Gemini. You need to check the scope to which your settings apply.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Judgment before input is the strongest control.
Sensitive information is classified and de-identified, leaving only the necessary columns.
Administrator controls only determine access; they do not determine input for you.
We share the results after confirming that no individual is revived.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for self-thinking purposes only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: What sensitivity level does my work data belong to, and what can I screen before entering it?
